from collections import defaultdict
data = defaultdict(list)
with open(VALUES_CSV) as f:
    r=csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in r:
        data[row['timeseries_id']].append((row['timestamp'],float(row['value'])))

# F3_Z01 setpoints
cool='5b98cbc1-fd25-5d8c-a96e-c3de49819174'
heat='b7f22e0c-833d-5373-87e1-51e1cb26f038'
for label,tid in [('coolingSP',cool),('heatingSP',heat)]:
    vs=[v for _,v in data[tid]]
    print(label,"unique",sorted(set(round(x,2) for x in vs))[:10], "n=",len(vs))
    print("  first",data[tid][0],"last",data[tid][-1])
# Check whether the setpoint tracks temp changes over time (i.e., a constant vs following season)
months=defaultdict(list)
for ts,v in data[cool]: months[ts[:7]].append(v)
print("coolSP monthly", {m:round(sum(v)/len(v),2) for m,v in sorted(months.items())})

content.text: The setpoints are essentially constant (cooling SP ~25.2°C all year, heating ~15.6–17°C no meaningful shift). The temperature of F3_Z01 rose ~+0.64°C after July 2018. Critically, the neighboring same-floor zones F3_Z02, F3_Z03, and F3_Z05 all rose in the same direction (~+0.5 to +0.6°C) over the same period, with constant setpoints. A single zone-sensor fault would show a step/drift in F3_Z01 only while same-floor neighbors stayed flat; instead the whole zone region tracks together, which is consistent with a genuine local load change rather than a sensor fault in F3_Z01's monitoring sensor.
